newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China fertiliser company plans Hong Kong listing.
newsitem.headline: China fertiliser company plans Hong Kong listing.

text.p: China's Sichuan Chuandong Group Co, which produces fertiliser, plans to raise 600 million yuan through an initial public offering in Hong Kong later this year, a source close to the issuer said on Wednesday.
The company will offer H shares -- stock of mainland Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong -- in the second half of 1997, the source told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Chuandong plans to use the proceeds from the issue to improve its fertiliser production technology, the source said.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission, the country's stock market watchdog, has already granted approval for the firm to list shares overseas, he said.

Chuandong, located in southwest Sichuan province's capital of Chengdu, expects urea output to reach 600,000 tonnes in 1997 compared with 520,000 tonnes in 1996, the source said. Urea is a key ingredient in some fertilisers.
Chuandong assets are now undergoing restructuring in preparation for the listing, he said. Hong Kong currently has 26 H shares trading on the exchange.
